answer.evidence: Rows 0-47 are an inclined ramp plane with chevron strokes pointing up the slope (north). A dark outline runs down the left edge and along the bottom of the slope at row 47. Dark wall strips on the left and right sides (about x 0-11 and x 44-47) show the cut cliff sides. Rows 48-63 are a uniform flat floor with scattered specks, not a vertical face. No vertical south face of 3 or more rows sits below the ramp surface. The ramp therefore reads as a sloped top-down surface with side walls, not as a front-elevation wall.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has a herringbone chevron ramp with tinted dark-brown side walls. Only 20% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is dark_material_tone rather than sticker black. Its visible tones per tile (7) match the paving reference (7) and exceed the grass reference (3). Against that, it has only 11 distinct colours in total, so each material ramp is shallow at about 4 steps against 5-6 in Beodeul. Near-flat coverage is 21% against 0% for both references. The sandy strip at the bottom and the dark side walls read as large, almost flat fills with little grain or per-stone shading. The ramp surface is also more uniform than the one-by-one shaded cobbles in the paving reference. It is clean and coherent but a little thinner and flatter than the references. Given the flat-fill coverage and the instruction to fail when in doubt, it fails.
